first.rationale: Onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%) are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (memory_31 signup field reduction, memory_86 onboarding shortening) point to the same lever with durable, low-risk lift in self-serve activation. This directly targets the observed metric declines without altering price/value perception. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but matching on price risks attracting exactly the price-sensitive, low-loyalty segment the competitor is targeting, which could erode long-term qualified revenue even if it shows short-term acquisition lift — flagging this as a risk to watch rather than acting on it now. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist are not clearly matched to the current SMB-facing metric drops. Given only one experiment slot and a live competitive shock that changes context since the original onboarding studies were run, I want to verify both onboarding-related memories before committing, and run this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout to check that the historical lift still holds under current market pressure.
